text:
anya: ran multi-gpu perf pass on the 8xA100 pool. seeing weird tail latency spikes when group_size=2 and tensor-parallel=4. attached perfbot summary below.
perfbot: profile attached: /perf/runs/1754003210/summary.html (CPU/GPU timelines, nvprof traces)
anya: main symptom: sustained all-reduce stalls at step boundaries, but compute utilization is high otherwise.
jiang: did you try forcing LL128? which nccl algos are being selected?
anya: default was AUTO -> proto for large messages. i re-ran with NCCL_ALGO=LL128 and NCCL_PROTO=LL128 for testing. reduced 95p by ~18% but throughput dropped slightly.
dmitri: interesting. can you paste the micro-profile for a single iteration where stall occurs? the timeline looked like two ranks waiting on recv for ~6ms.
anya: pasted snippet: ```
# timeline (ms)
0.0: compute fwd
1.2: kv-cache update (allgather 12KB)
1.4: tensor split + allreduce (128KB)
7.6: wait stall -> recv not posted
14.0: compute backward
```
katie: who owns the KV cache flush code? those 12KB allgathers at every token could be the noise — uneven sequence lengths mean more frequent small collectives.
anya: KV cache is in runtime/kv_cache.cpp, updated per token for streaming sessions. workload had 50% long convs and 50% short. batching heuristics coalesced mixed lengths into same batch.
jiang: aha — mixed-length batching causing many small allreduces interleaved with big ones. small collectives are sensitive to algorithm/proto and channel mapping.
nccldev: FYI, proto vs algo selection: SMALL <-> LL, MEDIUM <-> LL128, LARGE <-> TREE/RING depending on ring size. channels also matter — if you map channels by socket incorrectly, cross-socket BW suffers.
dmitri: can you try two experiments: 1) enforce per-batch length bucketing (split short/long) so small allreduces group together; 2) pin NCCL_CHANS_PER_SOCKET=2 and NCCL_LL=1 with NCCL_ALGO=RING for medium messages.
anya: started experiment 1 locally; split batches by max_seq<=64 and >64. early results: stall count down by 40%, 95p down 25%.
jiang: for experiment 2, weirdly RING gave better overlap with compute on our layout. maybe because our tensor-parallel group reduces cross-socket jumps.
perfbot: perf artifacts: run/1754003210/exp1_bucketed.tgz uploaded. run/1754003210/exp2_ring.tgz uploaded.
katie: do we have kernel-selection logs? hoping to see if some kernels are serialized by the runtime when using LL128 path.
anya: yes, runtime emitted kernel map for the run: ```
selected_kernels: attention_fwd: opt_v2
matmul_bwd: quantized_gemm_x8
allreduce_kernel: nccl_ll128_path
```
dmitri: opt_v2 attention has an extra workspace sync before KV update — that could push the timing and make allreduce land at bad points. try scheduling the KV allgather earlier (prefetch) so it can overlap with attention workspace sync.
anya: re-ordered KV update to prefetch in background thread and re-ran. latency tail improved another ~10%.
nccldev: another knob: NCCL_TOPO_ENABLE=1 to let nccl favor intra-socket rings for small collectives. also try NCCL_MAX_OPS or tuning comm/compute streams mapping.
jiang: agree. also consider combining small KV allgathers into one coalesced message at runtime if seqs are similar — reduces #collectives.
sre-bot: note created INCIDENT-2025-042: "nccl small-collective spikes on 8xA100" for tracking customer impact.
katie: next steps: 1) add length-bucketing to batching heuristics (low risk), 2) KV prefetch change + coalescing (medium risk), 3) run systematic NCCL channel/ALGO matrix on CI pools (high cost). volunteers?
dmitri: i can own CI matrix (need access to perf pool).
ccldev: i can help script NCCL env permutations and analyze per-rank timelines.
jiang: i'll open a PR for bucketing heuristics and include a perf test.
anya: thanks all — i'll attach the perf links and PR numbers once ready. :thumbsup:
